developers_seoDescription: Build on DXRating's maimai DX data: connect an AI assistant to the MCP server, or call the public REST API.
developers_description: maimai DX songs, charts and internal levels, for AI assistants and your own code.
developers_mcp_description: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or any MCP client. Search songs, look up charts and calculate ratings, no code needed.
developers_api_description: Start with dxdata: every song, chart, internal level, tag and alias in one cacheable JSON document. No account or API key needed.
developers_terms_dataDescription: Free to use, including commercially. Credit is appreciated. Song titles, artwork and charts belong to SEGA and their rights holders; DXRating claims no copyright over them.
developers_terms_limitsDescription: MCP: about 300 requests per minute per client. REST API: no hard limit, but cache responses and revalidate with If-None-Match. dxdata, tags, aliases and arcade venues send ETags.
developers_copyFailed: Couldn’t copy. Select the URL and copy it by hand.
developers_policy_intro: API v1 is stable. If you build a tool, bot or site on it, this is what you can rely on.
developers_policy_compatDescription: Within v1, changes are additive only: new endpoints, optional parameters, response fields and enum values. Ignore fields and values you don't recognise. Removing or renaming anything, or changing a type or meaning, counts as breaking. Correcting data (internal levels, titles, dates, server availability) does not.
developers_policy_deprecationDescription: Anything we retire gets at least 6 months' notice. It's announced in the changelog, and responses carry Deprecation (RFC 9745) and Sunset (RFC 8594) headers until it's gone.
developers_policy_versionsDescription: Breaking changes go into a new version at /api/v2. v1 keeps working for at least 12 months after v2 is stable.
developers_policy_idsDescription: Song IDs (dsng_…) and sheet IDs (dsht_…) are permanent and never reused. Songs and charts removed from the game stay in the catalog with an empty serverIds list. If two entries turn out to be the same song, one ID is kept and the other is never reused; a split keeps the original ID and adds a new one. Both are announced in the changelog.
developers_policy_scopeDescription: Covered: dxdata, tags, aliases and arcades, which need no sign-in. Trending and chart images are best-effort. Endpoints that need a DXRating account (comments, tag attaching, alias submission, score import) are for DXRating's own apps and can change at any time.
developers_policy_updatesDescription: Subscribe to the changelog issue on GitHub to get an email for every new field, endpoint and deprecation.
developers_policy_supportDescription: Questions, bugs and requests go to GitHub issues.

auth_privacy_intro_body: This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, process, and disclose your information when you use our service.
auth_privacy_collect_body: We collect information in the following ways:
auth_privacy_collect_direct_label: Information you provide to us directly:
auth_privacy_collect_direct_body: Information that you submit through our service, including registration information, profile information, and any other information you choose to provide.
auth_privacy_collect_usage_body: We collect information about your interactions with our service using PostHog analytics, including:
auth_privacy_collect_usage_item5: Technical information about your device and internet connection
auth_privacy_use_body: We use the collected information for various purposes:
auth_privacy_use_item1: To provide and maintain our service
auth_privacy_use_item2: To notify you about changes to our service
auth_privacy_use_item4: To monitor usage of our service
auth_privacy_use_item5: To detect, prevent, and address technical issues
auth_privacy_storage_body: We use a secure database provider. Your data is stored securely and processed in accordance with security standards and practices.
auth_privacy_analytics_body: We use PostHog, an open-source analytics platform, to understand how our service is used. PostHog collects anonymous usage data that helps us improve our service. You can learn more about PostHog's privacy practices on their website.
auth_privacy_mcp_body: When an AI assistant uses our MCP server (mcp.dxrating.net), we record the tool called and its arguments, including search text, the client app (name, version and User-Agent), your IP address and approximate location (country). These records go to our error and monitoring provider, Sentry, and are kept under its retention. We also send anonymous usage analytics to PostHog without the IP address and without person profiles; there, search text is cut to 64 characters, email addresses and long numbers are removed, and scores are never included.
auth_privacy_cookies_body: We use cookies and similar tracking technologies to track activity on our service and hold certain information. You can instruct your browser to refuse all cookies or to indicate when a cookie is being sent.
auth_privacy_retention_body: We will retain your information only for as long as necessary to fulfill the purposes outlined in this Privacy Policy. We will retain and use your information to the extent necessary to comply with our legal obligations, resolve disputes, and enforce our policies.
auth_privacy_deletion_p1: You can permanently delete your account from the account screen in the DXRating app. Deletion removes your profile, comments, tags and tag attachments, aliases, sessions, passkeys, linked sign-in methods, and linked LXNS credentials. Linked OAuth grants are revoked when supported by the provider. After deletion, you can create a new account using the same email address or sign-in provider.
auth_privacy_deletion_p2: Account data is removed from our active systems immediately. Residual copies may remain in encrypted backups until those backups are automatically deleted, or when retention is required by law.
auth_privacy_rights_body: You have the following data protection rights:
auth_privacy_rights_item1: The right to access, update, or delete your information
auth_privacy_changes_body: We may update our Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of any changes by posting the new Privacy Policy on this page and updating the "Last updated" date.

constants_seoDescription: All {count} maimai DX Lv.{level} charts by internal level ({min}–{max}), with SSS+ / SSS rating, notes and version.
constants_intro: {count} DX and Standard charts at level {level}, from internal level {max} down to {min}. The rating columns show the single-chart rating at 100.5% (SSS+) and 100.0% (SSS).
constants_index_seoTitle: maimai DX Internal Level (Constant) Tables by Level
constants_index_seoDescription: maimai DX internal level (chart constant) tables for every level from 10 to 15, with single-chart ratings at SSS+ and SSS.
constants_index_intro: Pick a level to see every chart sorted by internal level.
ratingExplainer_intro: Your maimai DX rating is the sum of the single-chart ratings of your 50 best plays: 15 from charts added in the current version (B15) and 35 from all older charts (B35). This page calculates it from your scores; the rules below are what it uses.
ratingExplainer_formula_body: Single-chart rating = ⌊ internal level × min(achievement, 100.5%) × rank coefficient ⌋. The internal level (chart constant) is the decimal behind the displayed level, e.g. a 14+ chart can be 14.6 to 14.9. An all perfect (AP or AP+) adds 1.
ratingExplainer_example_body: A {constant} chart cleared at 100.5% (SSS+) gives ⌊{constant} × 1.005 × 22.4⌋ = {sssp}. At 100.0% (SSS) it gives {sss}, and at 99.5% (SS+) {ssp}.
ratingExplainer_constants_link: Find charts worth playing in the internal level tables →
ratingExplainer_faq_a1: The 50 plays that make up your rating: your best 15 charts from the current version plus your best 35 from older versions. Raising a play that is outside the 50 does not change your rating until it beats the lowest entry in its bucket.
ratingExplainer_faq_q2: Where do internal levels come from?
ratingExplainer_faq_a2: DXRating's catalog collects the internal levels for every chart on the Japanese, international and Chinese servers and updates them daily. Each chart page also shows how its internal level changed across versions.
ratingExplainer_faq_q3: How do I add my scores?
ratingExplainer_faq_a3: Import them from maimai DX NET or LXNS, or add charts by hand from the search. Scores stay in your browser unless you sign in.
ratingExplainer_faq_q4: Why is my in-game rating different?
ratingExplainer_faq_a4: Check that the selected version and server match the game. New-version charts only count toward B15 in the version they were added in, and internal levels can change between versions.

tools_tolerance_seoTitle: maimai DX Score Tolerance Calculator (GREAT / GOOD / MISS allowance)
tools_tolerance_seoDescription: Find out how many GREATs, GOODs and MISSes a maimai DX chart allows for a target achievement such as SSS+ (100.5%), per note type, with BREAK 50 / 100 equivalents.
tools_tolerance_intro: Pick a chart and a target achievement to see how many non-perfect judgements you can afford.
tools_tolerance_sectionIntro: How many judgements you can lose and still reach the target. Each count assumes every other note is perfect.
tools_tolerance_footnote: BREAK drops only cost bonus score. A BREAK GREAT or worse costs much more.
tools_tolerance_noNoteCounts: Note counts for this chart are not available yet.
tools_tolerance_pickAChart: Search for a song above and choose a chart.
tools_rating_seoTitle: maimai DX Single-Chart Rating Calculator (Internal Level × Achievement)
tools_rating_seoDescription: Single-chart rating calculator for maimai DX: get the rating one chart awards from its internal level and achievement, reverse it to the achievement a target rating needs, and browse a rating table per internal level.
tools_rating_intro: Rating for a single chart, the achievement a rating needs, and a rating table by internal level.
tools_rating_targetInvalid: Enter a whole number, such as 280
tools_rating_forward_description: The rating a chart awards for an achievement, without the AP bonus.
tools_rating_reverse_description: The lowest achievement that awards at least the target rating.
tools_rating_table_description: Ratings at each rank for the chosen internal level and its neighbours.
tools_tolerance_sheetSeoDescription: How many GREAT, GOOD and MISS you can afford on {title} {sheetLabel} and still reach SSS+ or any target achievement, per note type, with BREAK 50 / 100 conversions.
recommend_description: Charts where the next achievement step adds the most rating to your Best 50.
recommend_demo: Showing demo scores, not your own records.
recommend_empty: Import your scores to see which charts raise your rating the most.
recommend_none: Nothing to raise here right now.
random_description: Pick a random chart by type, difficulty, level and version.
random_range_spanHint: Tap another level to select everything in between.
